Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when the code is executed

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration assumes rows exist in `site_settings` and immediately indexes into the first row: `execute(...)[0]['id']` and later `execute(...)[0]['value']`. If the `embed_category` (or `uncategorized_category_id`) setting was never persisted in the `site_settings` table (common since defaults may not be stored), `execute(...)[0]` returns `nil`, and `nil['id']`/`nil['value']` raises a NoMethodError. This is a concrete crash path introduced by the migration logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer) runs an uncached, non-memoized DB query (WHERE lower(host) = ?) on every request to the hot public /embed/comments endpoint, regressing from the free in-memory SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? check

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the public embed path validation from `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?(request.referer)` to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`). `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host`, which executes `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, i.e., a DB query per call, with no caching/memoization shown. By contrast, the removed `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` checked an in-memory site setting string (typically cached), so this is a verifiable per-request DB lookup regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The embeddable_hosts migration creates no index on the host column, and the lower(host) comparison would require a functional index on lower(host) (or normalized lowercase storage) to be used, causing sequential scans on the hot path

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with `host` and `category_id` but adds no indexes. Lookup on the request path uses `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, which queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`. With no index on `host` (and especially with a function applied to the column), the database cannot use an efficient index lookup and will fall back to scanning the table as it grows. This lookup is used in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, i.e., on embed requests, so it’s a concrete performance defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin embedding endpoint materializes all EmbeddableHost rows unpaginated via EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host) with no limit, serialized wholesale into the payload

adjudication.rationale: The diff does indeed load all rows via `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` in `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding`, and the serializer (`EmbeddingSerializer` with `has_many :embeddable_hosts`) will include the full list in the response. However, the finding frames this as a definite defect (“problem”) due to lack of pagination/limit; that’s a performance/scalability concern without evidence in the diff that pagination is required or that the dataset is expected to be large. In an admin settings screen, returning the full list can be intentional and reasonable. لذا it’s verifiable behavior but not a clear bug/security/correctness issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError on installs that never customized embed_category, because Discourse only persists site setting rows when they deviate from default, so the SELECT returns zero rows and [0] is nil, blocking deploys
Migration uses unparameterized SQL string interpolation for host values in the INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts statement, breaking the INSERT when a host value contains a quote

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. If any existing `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` entry contains a single quote (or other SQL-special characters), the generated SQL becomes syntactically invalid and the migration will fail. This is directly verifiable from the diff and is a correctness defect (and also an injection risk, albeit from internal data).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Data migration crashes with NoMethodError when the 'embed_category' site setting row doesn't exist (fresh installs), because the unguarded [0]['id'] lookup returns nil
The uncategorized_category_id fallback lookup in the migration has the same unguarded [0]['value'] pattern that can raise on nil

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, the fallback does `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i`. If that SELECT returns zero rows, `execute(...)[0]` is `nil`, and indexing `['value']` will raise (e.g., `NoMethodError`). This is an unguarded access pattern present in the diff (and similarly also exists earlier with `[0]['id']`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin embeddable_hosts update and destroy raise NoMethodError (500) on nil when the id is unknown instead of returning 404
save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host][:host] unconditionally, so a request missing that envelope raises a 500 instead of a 400/422

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` without checking that `params[:embeddable_host]` is present. If a client sends a malformed request (e.g., missing the `embeddable_host` envelope), `params[:embeddable_host]` will be `nil` and Ruby will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil:NilClass`, producing a 500 rather than a handled 4xx validation/error response. There is no `require`/`permit` or guard in the diff to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store.js plural hydration branch throws if the serialized *_ids value is null (obj[k].map on null)

hydrated || [] is dead code in store.js hydration; failed lookups produce [undefined, ...] garbage entries and foo_ids is unconditionally deleted, mutating/degrading the payload shape for all store consumers instead of keeping raw ids when no side-loaded records exist

adjudication.rationale: In store.js `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new `_ids` branch does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` and then assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` and *always* `delete obj[k]`. Since `Array#map` always returns an array, `hydrated || []` is effectively dead code. More importantly, if `_lookupSubType(...)` can’t find a sideloaded record for an id, the mapped array will contain `undefined` entries (e.g. `[undefined, ...]`), yet `foo_ids` is still deleted unconditionally. This is a behavior change from the `_id` branch, which only deletes the raw id when hydration succeeds, so the finding about payload shape being degraded (raw ids removed even when hydration fails) is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a silent no-op that returns 200 with the unchanged record, never reading or persisting any params

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` just re-renders `@embedding` and never reads `params` or persists anything. `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` with `id: 'default'` and `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all...`, so there is nothing being modified on PUT `/admin/customize/embedding`. This makes the update endpoint a no-op that will return success with unchanged data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of embeddable_hosts/embed_category settings from site_settings.yml and DB deletion in the same migration breaks external consumers with no deprecation window

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings (from `config/site_settings.yml`) and the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` explicitly deletes those rows from `site_settings` after importing data into the new `embeddable_hosts` table. However, the claimed “breaks external consumers with no deprecation window” is not a verifiable defect within this diff: all in-repo references to those settings are removed/rewired to `EmbeddableHost` (e.g., `EmbedController`, `TopicEmbed`, `Topic#expandable_first_post?`, `TopicRetriever`). Any breakage to *external* code/plugins is speculative and not provable from the diff alone, and the change appears to be an intentional migration/feature refactor rather than an internal correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Category model lacks has_many :embeddable_hosts with dependent handling, so deleting a category leaves embeddable host rows pointing at a nonexistent category id

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces EmbeddableHost with a `belongs_to :category` and a non-null `category_id` column, but it does not show the `Category` model at all. The proposed finding claims the Category model “lacks has_many :embeddable_hosts with dependent handling”, which cannot be verified from this diff. While it’s true there is no DB-level foreign key or explicit cleanup/reassignment logic shown here for when a category is deleted, concluding that Category deletion will leave orphaned embeddable_host rows depends on code not present in the diff (Category destroy behavior/constraints).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller doesn't validate that the submitted category_id refers to an existing category

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code assigns `host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` (or uncategorized if blank) and then saves. There is no check that the provided `category_id` exists, and the `embeddable_hosts` table migration adds `category_id` as `null: false` but does not add a foreign key constraint. The `EmbeddableHost` model also has `belongs_to :category` without a presence/existence validation. So a crafted request can persist an `EmbeddableHost` pointing to a nonexistent category, creating an integrity/correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration SQL INSERT uses string interpolation for host values, so a single quote in legacy data breaks the migration

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, legacy hosts are read from the site_settings value, split into lines, and inserted via raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If any legacy line `h` contains a single quote (`'`), the generated SQL becomes invalid (unterminated string) and the migration can fail. There is no escaping/quoting helper used here (e.g., `quote(h)`), so the finding is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category setting is absent or empty: `[0]['id']` on an empty result set returns nil and `nil['id']` raises, aborting the migration before the fallback is reached

adjudication.rationale:
In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does:

category_id = execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i

If there is no matching site_settings row for embed_category, or it doesn't join to a category (e.g. empty/invalid), the SQL result set is empty. In that case `[0]` returns `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration before the subsequent fallback (`if category_id == 0 ...`) can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration INSERT uses unescaped string interpolation for host values, causing SQL syntax errors on quotes; also nil category_id from a missing uncategorized category lookup makes the INSERT syntactically invalid

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, host values are interpolated directly into SQL: `VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)` with no escaping/quoting helper. If any stored `embeddable_hosts` line contains a single-quote (or other SQL-special chars), this will break the SQL and is also an injection risk during migration.

Also, the category lookup can fail before the intended fallback: `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` assumes the SELECT returns at least one row. If there is no `site_settings` row for `embed_category` (common if settings are only persisted when overridden) or it doesn’t match a category, `[0]` is `nil` and the migration will raise `NoMethodError` (so you don’t even reach the `category_id == 0` fallback). The finding’s “nil makes INSERT syntactically invalid” is slightly off (it’s more likely a Ruby exception), but it correctly identifies a real defect in the migration logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy raise NoMethodError on nil when the record doesn't exist (stale tab, concurrent edits), producing a 500 instead of a 404; missing params[:embeddable_host] also raises

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb, both #update and #destroy fetch with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately call `save_host(host)` or `host.destroy` without checking for nil. If the record doesn’t exist, `save_host` calls `host.host = ...` and will raise NoMethodError, and `host.destroy` will also raise, yielding a 500 instead of a 404. Additionally, `save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `[:category_id]` without guarding against a missing `:embeddable_host` key, which would also raise NoMethodError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost before_validation crashes with NoMethodError on nil host (API call omitting host key), producing a 500 instead of a 422 validation error
No category existence validation on EmbeddableHost allows stale category_id after category deletion, causing TopicEmbed.import to create topics with non-existent category and frontend null rendering
Frontend destroyRecord has no .catch failure handler, so failed destroy requests (e.g., server 500) silently leave the row with no user feedback

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... });` but does not attach a `.catch(...)` (unlike `save()`, which uses `.catch(popupAjaxError)`). If the DELETE request fails (e.g., 500/network), the rejection is unhandled and no user-facing error is shown, so the UI provides no feedback and the row remains without explanation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a silent no-op that persists nothing while the client reports success on save, since fetch_embedding builds an OpenStruct with nothing to persist

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::EmbeddingController`, `fetch_embedding` builds `@embedding` as an `OpenStruct` (`id: 'default'`, `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all...`), not an AR model. The `update` action ignores params and only `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`, so a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` will always return success without persisting any changes. The client side also defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would hit this no-op endpoint and appear successful because the server responds with serialized data regardless of changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New controller specs for admin/embeddable_hosts_controller and admin/embedding_controller only verify class ancestry (Controller < Admin::AdminController) with zero behavioral coverage for create/update happy path, validation failure, blank category_id fallback, or destroy

adjudication.rationale: The two new spec files `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` each contain only a single example asserting the controller is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`, and do not exercise any controller actions (`create`, `update`, `destroy`, `show`) or edge cases like validation errors or the `category_id` fallback logic in `save_host`. This is directly verifiable from the diff; the added tests provide essentially no behavioral coverage for the newly introduced controllers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update with a nonexistent id: EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil and save_host calls host.host = ... on nil, raising NoMethodError and a 500

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb#update, it does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately calls `save_host(host)`. `save_host` unconditionally dereferences `host` (`host.host = ...`, `host.category_id = ...`), so if no record exists for the given id, `host` will be nil and this will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 instead of a 404/handled error. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff; there is no nil-guard.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Data migration copies hosts verbatim from the old embeddable_hosts setting without stripping the scheme, so migrated rows like 'http://discourse.org' never match the lower(host) = uri.host lookup, silently breaking embeds post-migration

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration copies each line from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting directly into the `embeddable_hosts.host` column via raw SQL: `INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. This bypasses the `EmbeddableHost` model `before_validation` callback that strips `http://`/`https://` and paths. Later, host checks use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` which parses the incoming URL and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. If the migrated row is stored as `http://discourse.org` (or includes a path), it will not match `uri.host` (`discourse.org`), so previously-allowed hosts can become disallowed after migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration raises NoMethodError on fresh install when no embed_category row exists in site_settings, breaking rake db:migrate from scratch

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `category_id = execute("SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If that query returns zero rows (likely on a fresh install, since this diff removes `embed_category` from `config/site_settings.yml`, so there may be no `site_settings` row named `embed_category`), then `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, breaking `rake db:migrate` from scratch. The later `if category_id == 0` fallback won’t run because the exception happens first.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration uses raw string-interpolated INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...) which produces broken SQL if a host value contains a quote

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration iterates over host strings from the existing `site_settings` value and executes raw SQL built via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Because `h` is inserted inside single quotes without any escaping/quoting helper, any host value containing a single quote (or other SQL-special characters) will produce invalid SQL and can potentially alter the statement. This is a concrete correctness/safety issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#show has no request test; the OpenStruct + embed: :ids serialization path (which may fail because OpenStruct doesn't define embeddable_host_ids) and the JSON payload shape the Ember frontend depends on are never validated
Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that re-renders without saving anything, and no test would reveal that

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads params or persists any changes. `@embedding` is built in `fetch_embedding` as an `OpenStruct` with `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`, so there is nothing to save anyway. On the client side, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines an action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would hit the PUT `/admin/customize/embedding` route, but that route's controller action is a no-op. The provided specs for `Admin::EmbeddingController` only assert inheritance and would not catch that update does not perform any persistence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: JS store test asserts the wrong fruit's colors because the pretender handler for /fruits/:id returns fruits[0] unconditionally, so the test verifies the mock rather than actual behavior

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding refers to a "JS store test" involving "fruits" and a Pretender handler for "/fruits/:id" returning `fruits[0]` unconditionally. Nothing in the provided diff contains any fruit-related code, Pretender handlers, or such a test. adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import behavior change from SiteSetting.embed_category to EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url).try(:category_id) means importing from an unmatched host creates a topic with no category, and there is no test covering this edge case

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `TopicEmbed.import` to use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url).try(:category_id)` instead of `SiteSetting.embed_category`. However, the embedding flow in this same diff now enforces host allowlisting via `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` in both `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`. For any URL that reaches `TopicEmbed.import` through the intended embedding paths, `record_for_host(url)` should return a matching `EmbeddableHost` (and `category_id` is non-null on that table), so the “unmatched host creates a topic with no category” case is not a verifiable bug introduced by this diff. The “no test covering this edge case” part is also about test completeness rather than a concrete defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No negative test for embeddable_host host format validation; every model spec feeds valid input, so invalid hosts failing validation (the path render_json_error depends on) are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `EmbeddableHost` format validation (`validates_format_of :host, ...`) and the accompanying spec (`spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb`) only exercises valid inputs (http/https/path trimming and host_allowed? with known-good hosts). There is indeed no test asserting invalid hosts are rejected, nor any controller spec covering the `render_json_error(host)` path when validation fails. However, this is a test-coverage gap rather than a verifiable functional/correctness defect introduced by the diff; the validation itself is present and will fail invalid inputs regardless of the missing test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? test outside the 'with an embeddable host' context passes trivially because has_topic_embed? is unstubbably false, and the removed SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? condition has no test documenting the new truncation behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `Topic#expandable_first_post?` by removing the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` guard, but the proposed finding is primarily about the adequacy/structure of a spec (“test … passes trivially …” and lack of documentation/coverage). In the provided diff, the `expandable_first_post?` spec section is truncated/incomplete, so the claim about a specific test context passing trivially cannot be verified from what’s shown. Also, “no test documenting the new truncation behavior” is a test-coverage critique rather than a clear functional defect introduced by the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _hydrateEmbedded plural branch calls obj[k].map(...) directly and throws 'Cannot read property map of null' if a serializer emits null ids; also unsanitized null/undefined entries from failed _lookupSubType; no tests exercise empty or missing ids

adjudication.rationale: In store.js.es6, _hydrateEmbedded was changed to also process keys ending in `_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` and, when plural (`m[2]` truthy), it unconditionally does `obj[k].map(function(id) { ... })`. If the payload contains `something_ids: null` (or any non-array), this will throw at runtime (`null.map` / `undefined.map`). The new code also does not filter results of `_lookupSubType`; if lookup fails it will insert `null/undefined` into the hydrated array, and `hydrated || []` won’t remove those because an array is always truthy. The diff adds no guarding/tests for empty/missing/null `_ids` fields, so this is a real fragility introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator definitions were swapped between files: embeddable_host fabricator is in category_fabricator.rb and category fabricators are in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
Ember frontend for the embedding admin page shipped with no component or acceptance tests

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when the embed_category site setting has no DB row, because the query returns zero rows and [0]['id'] is called on nil (missing guard for fresh installs)
Fabricator files have been swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains only the embeddable_host fabricator while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all the category fabricators
Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that re-serializes the same OpenStruct without persisting anything, and the frontend saveChanges action is dead code never invoked by any template

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController update and destroy raise NoMethodError (500) when the record id doesn't exist, missing standard not-found handling
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue describe that update/destroy fetch an EmbeddableHost by id without handling the nil case, leading to a NoMethodError/500 when the record is not found.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Destructive non-reversible migration written as change: irreversible DELETE of site_settings with no up/down reversal, plus raw string-interpolated INSERTs that break on values containing quotes and are an injection-shaped hazard

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration uses `def change` but performs irreversible operations via raw `execute`, including `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"` with no `up/down` or `reversible` block to restore data on rollback. Also, it builds SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`; if `h` contains a single quote it will break the SQL, and because `h` ultimately comes from a DB setting value, this is an injection-shaped hazard (not safely parameterized/quoted).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fake model via OpenStruct with id 'default' serialized by EmbeddingSerializer — no Embedding model exists, leaking controller-owned persistence shape into serialization

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding` building `@embedding` as an `OpenStruct` with `id: 'default'` and serializing it via `EmbeddingSerializer`, and there is no Rails `Embedding` model added. However, this is not a verifiable defect by itself: Discourse serializers commonly serialize non-AR objects, and `EmbeddingSerializer` only needs `id` and `embeddable_hosts`, which the `OpenStruct` provides. The frontend also adds an Ember adapter for `embedding` pointing at `/admin/customize/embedding`, so the lack of a persisted model isn’t inherently broken. The finding reads as an architectural/style concern rather than a clear bug/security/correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead method overrides in serializers: id/host/category_id methods merely restate what ApplicationSerializer already does for declared attributes

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbeddableHostSerializer` declares `attributes :id, :host, :category_id` and then defines `id`, `host`, and `category_id` methods that simply return `object.<attr>`. Likewise `EmbeddingSerializer` declares `attributes :id` and defines `id` returning `object.id`. These overrides are redundant, but they are not a verifiable defect (no correctness/security bug introduced); they still return the same values and won’t break serialization. This is a maintainability/style nit, not a real problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code and null leaks in plural hydration branch in store.js.es6: '|| []' after map is dead code, and null entries from _lookupSubType are silently included in the array unlike the singular branch's guard

adjudication.rationale: In the new plural hydration branch in `store.js.es6`, `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` will always return an Array, so `hydrated || []` is indeed unreachable/dead code. Also, unlike the singular `_id` branch (which only assigns `obj[subType]` when `hydrated` is truthy), the plural `_ids` branch assigns the mapped array verbatim, so any `null/undefined` results from `_lookupSubType` will be included as array elements with no filtering/guard. This behavioral difference is present in the diff and can lead to null entries in the hydrated collection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unused i18n key admin.embedding.edit is never referenced by any template or component

The templates use `admin.embedding.title`, `admin.embedding.host`, `admin.embedding.category`, `admin.embedding.add_host`, and JS uses `admin.embedding.confirm_delete`, but there is no `{{i18n "admin.embedding.edit"}}` or `I18n.t('admin.embedding.edit')` anywhere in the diff. So the key appears unused.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Global coupling and undefined-category risk in embeddable-host component save action: reaching into Discourse.Category registry diverges from server behavior (which coerces to uncategorized_category_id), causing table to render out of sync until reload
Misleading leftover test name 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' fabricates no host and passes only because embed_truncate defaults false, not because of host state

However, the proposed finding is specifically about a leftover/misleading *test name* ('is false if embeddable_host is blank') and a test that fabricates no host; that test content/name is not present in the provided diff snippet (the `topic_spec` section is truncated before any such example is shown). Without the actual test in the diff, this claim isn’t verifiable from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when the 'embed_category' site setting row is absent (site never changed it from default), because [0] is nil and nil['id'] raises before the category_id == 0 fallback is reached
matched_golden_ids: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the migration assumes execute(...)[0] exists and immediately indexes into it for ['id'], which crashes with NoMethodError when the 'embed_category' site setting row is missing (no rows returned), before any fallback logic can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration also crashes if embed_category was set but the matching category was renamed or deleted, since the INNER JOIN drops out and [0] is nil

adjudication.rationale: Real issue in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb: it does `execute(... INNER JOIN site_settings ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category' )[0]['id'].to_i`. If the query returns zero rows (e.g., embed_category setting exists but no category has that name because it was renamed/deleted, or the setting is absent/blank), `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises, crashing the migration before the `category_id == 0` fallback can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Destructive DELETE of site settings rows ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category') inside a def change migration with no down method or rollback path, causing irreversible data loss

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses `def change` and ends with `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. There is no `down` method (or reversible block) to restore those site_settings rows on rollback, and the `execute` calls make the migration non-reversible by Rails. While some of the data is copied into the new `embeddable_hosts` table earlier in the migration, the original site setting records themselves are still permanently removed with no rollback path in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backfill copies raw host values (e.g. 'http://discourse.org') into embeddable_hosts.host without applying the model's normalization (stripping scheme and path), so migrated entries never match in record_for_host comparisons and embedding silently breaks

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` copies each line from the old `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` directly into the `embeddable_hosts.host` column via raw SQL (`INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), bypassing the `EmbeddableHost` model’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the incoming URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, so a migrated row stored as `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` will never match `discourse.org` / `example.com`, causing `host_allowed?` to return false and embedding to fail for those hosts. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw string interpolation of host values into the backfill INSERT SQL allows SQL injection or migration breakage from quotes/backslashes in stored values, since model quoting is bypassed
matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same underlying problem: SQL is constructed using raw string interpolation of host values (e.g., "#{h}"), bypassing proper quoting/parameterization and making it vulnerable to SQL injection (and also to breakage from special characters).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backfill inserts empty or whitespace-only lines from split("\n") as junk rows because model validation callbacks are bypassed

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the backfill reads the old SiteSetting value, does `records = val.split("\n")`, and then unconditionally executes an `INSERT` for each `h` without stripping or skipping blanks. If the setting contains blank lines, whitespace-only lines, or a trailing newline (which makes `split("\n")` include an empty string), it will insert rows with `host` as `''` or `'   '`. This uses raw SQL (`execute`) so the EmbeddableHost model’s validations and `before_validation` trimming callbacks are bypassed, leaving junk rows in the table.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table uses force: true, which silently drops and recreates a pre-existing embeddable_hosts table, losing data in partially-migrated or re-run scenarios

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration calls `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it. If this migration is re-run in a scenario where the table exists but the migration version isn’t recorded (e.g., a partially-failed migration run or manual/schema_migrations issues), it can silently delete existing `embeddable_hosts` data before repopulating, which is data-lossy behavior introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin controller update and destroy actions raise NoMethodError (500) when the embeddable host record is not found, instead of returning 404/error JSON

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController, both update and destroy fetch the record with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If no record exists, `host` is `nil`. `update` then calls `save_host(host)`, which immediately does `host.host = ...` and `host.category_id = ...`, raising `NoMethodError` on nil. `destroy` calls `host.destroy`, also raising `NoMethodError` when nil. There is no nil check or 404/error JSON handling, so a missing record will produce a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No unique index on embeddable_hosts.host, allowing duplicate rows and making the category applied to embedded topics nondeterministic since record_for_host uses .first

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with `host` and `category_id` but adds no unique index/constraint on `host`, and the model `EmbeddableHost` has no `validates_uniqueness_of`. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, so if duplicate rows exist for the same host, the chosen row (and thus `category_id` used in `TopicEmbed.import`) is dependent on database row ordering and is not deterministic. The admin UI also allows adding hosts without any duplicate prevention shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator file contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains the embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the category fabricators
matched_golden_ids: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly states that the contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped, which is the same underlying issue described in the golden comment (swapped files leading to loss/misplacement of expected fabricators and potential usage errors).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that never reads or applies params and returns success, creating a dead/misleading API surface

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action does not read `params` or modify any persisted state; it simply re-renders `@embedding` (an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`) via `EmbeddingSerializer`. Routes expose `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`, and the Ember admin controller calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, implying an updatable resource. As implemented, the endpoint always "succeeds" without applying any changes, which is a misleading/dead API surface.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes on installs that never changed embed_category: site_settings rows are lazily created, so the query returns zero rows and [0]['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration; same failure mode applies to the uncategorized_category_id lookup on line 14

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id']` for the `embed_category` lookup and later `execute(...)[0]['value']` for `uncategorized_category_id`. If those `SELECT` queries return 0 rows (which is plausible because Discourse stores many site_settings rows lazily only when changed from default), then `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` / `nil['value']` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration. The subsequent `if category_id == 0` check is never reached in that case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migrated hosts keep scheme/path in the host value (raw SQL insert bypasses the model's before_validation normalizer), so hosts recorded like 'http://eviltrout.com' or with paths silently fail host_allowed? against record_for_host's exact lower(host) = uri.host comparison, breaking embeds post-upgrade

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` copies `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` into the new `embeddable_hosts` table via raw SQL: `INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. This bypasses the `EmbeddableHost` model’s `before_validation` normalizer that strips `http(s)://` and paths. The new authorization check `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` calls `record_for_host`, which parses the referer and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. If the migrated DB value is `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://example.com/1234`, it will not equal `eviltrout.com` and the host will be rejected, breaking embeds post-upgrade for such stored values. The diff’s tests even fabricate hosts with schemes/paths (e.g., `Fabricate(:embeddable_host, host: 'https://example.com/1234')`), which would only work if normalization ran, further highlighting the mismatch when migration bypasses it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration resolves the embed category by joining s.value = c.name, but the setting stored a category id (as consumed by TopicEmbed.import), so the join finds nothing and embed topics silently fall back to uncategorized
Admin::EmbeddableHostsController update/destroy raise NoMethodError (500) instead of 404 when the id is stale/unknown because the nil record isn't handled

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch the record via `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If the id is stale/unknown, `first` returns `nil`. `update` then calls `save_host(host)` and `save_host` immediately does `host.host = ...` / `host.category_id = ...`, which will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil`. `destroy` similarly calls `host.destroy` on a possibly-nil `host`. There is no guard (e.g., `find` with exception handling or a 404 render), so this would produce a 500 instead of a 404/appropriate error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: save_host crashes with NoMethodError when embeddable_host params are missing (params[:embeddable_host][:host] nil dig) and a nil host value raises in before_validation's self.host.sub!, producing 500s instead of a 422 validation error
matched_golden_ids: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same root bug: a before_validation callback calls `self.host.sub!` and will raise `NoMethodError` when `host` is nil, leading to a crash (500) instead of a validation error. The candidate adds context about missing params, but the underlying issue matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation regex permits a port (:\d{1,5}) and before_validation strips only scheme/path, but record_for_host compares against uri.host which never includes a port, so hosts saved with a port like example.com:8080 can never match

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbeddableHost` validates `host` with a regex that explicitly allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`). The `before_validation` normalization strips only scheme (`/^https?:\/\//`) and path (`/\/.*$/`), but does not strip a `:port`, so a record can be saved as e.g. `example.com:8080`. However `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL via `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host` (hostname only, no port) for lookup: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. That means a saved `example.com:8080` will never match an incoming referer like `http://example.com:8080/...` because the lookup key becomes `example.com` while the stored value is `example.com:8080`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Plural hydration in store.js throws TypeError if a payload contains null for an *_ids key (obj[k].map on null)

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch matches keys like `*_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` and then unconditionally does `obj[k].map(function(id) { ... })`. If the server payload ever includes a `*_ids` field whose value is `null` (or otherwise non-array), this will raise a `TypeError` because `null`/`undefined` has no `map` method. There is no guard (e.g., `Array.isArray(obj[k])`) or defaulting before calling `map`, so the finding is a real defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Plural hydration branch assigns hydrated || [] unconditionally and injects a new obj[plural] property (potentially with null entries for non-side-loaded ids), and the regex now matches any key ending in _ids across all API payloads, not just intended ones

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, `_hydrateEmbedded` changes the key match from `/(.+)_id$/` to `/(.+)_id(s?)$/`, so *any* payload key ending in `_ids` will now be treated as an embedded association and the original key will be deleted. In the plural branch it always does `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` and `delete obj[k]`, but `hydrated` is always an array from `map` (even if `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined` for non-sideloaded ids), so you can end up with `groups: [undefined, ...]` (or similar) while losing the original `group_ids` field. This behavior applies globally to all API payloads processed by the store, not just the new embedding endpoints, and is a concrete correctness regression if any existing payloads legitimately include `_ids` fields that are not sideloaded relationships or are expected to remain as raw id lists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration SQL interpolates unescaped host values, so legacy hosts containing a single quote break the migration mid-way, leaving a half-migrated state

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration builds raw SQL with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If a legacy `embeddable_hosts` setting line `h` contains a single quote, the SQL string becomes invalid and the migration will error. The “half-migrated state” part is not guaranteed because Rails typically runs migrations in a transaction on PostgreSQL (so it would likely roll back), but the unescaped interpolation causing migration failure is a real defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that reports success (200) with no mutation, a silent-pass endpoint where future UI fields will 'save' nothing

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders `@embedding` (an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`) and performs no mutation/persistence based on request params. Yet a PUT route is added (`put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`) and the admin Ember controller defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would receive a 200/OK-like serialized response without saving anything. While the current template doesn’t invoke `saveChanges`, the endpoint itself is a verifiable no-op update that can silently “succeed” without changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation regex \.[a-z]{2,5} rejects TLDs longer than 5 characters (.museum, .technology) and hosts without a TLD (localhost), with no dev-mode bypass in TopicRetriever/TopicEmbed

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbeddableHost` with `validates_format_of :host, with: /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). This regex requires a dot and restricts the TLD to 2–5 letters, so it will reject valid modern TLDs longer than 5 (e.g. `.museum`, `.technology`) and also rejects hosts without a TLD like `localhost`. The diff also switches host checks from `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` in `TopicRetriever` and `TopicEmbed` without any development/admin bypass like the one that exists only in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, so these code paths will not accept such hosts even in dev/test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No uniqueness validation or unique index on host allows duplicate hosts with different categories, making the matched category nondeterministic (record_for_host uses .first with no order)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds the EmbeddableHost model and table but does not enforce uniqueness of `host`: the model only has `validates_format_of :host` (no `validates :host, uniqueness: ...`) and the migration `create_embeddable_hosts` creates no unique index/constraint on `host`. As a result, duplicate rows for the same host (possibly with different `category_id`) are allowed. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` with no ordering, so if duplicates exist the selected record (and thus category used in `TopicEmbed.import` via `eh.try(:category_id)`) is not reliably determined.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Frontend destroyRecord() has no .catch, so delete failures are silent and the row stays in the table with no error shown

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', this.get('host')); });` with no `.catch(...)`. If the backend delete fails (network/server/validation), the rejection is not handled here and no `popupAjaxError` (which is already imported and used for `save`) is shown. Also, because `deleteHost` is only sent on success, the row will remain in the table, matching the finding’s claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: After save() succeeds, Discourse.Category.findById returns undefined when categoryId is null, so the UI displays a blank category (disagreeing with the persisted uncategorized default) until reload

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, `categoryId` is initialized to `null` and only set in `edit()` (existing records) or via the `category-chooser` binding. For a new host, a user can save without choosing a category, so `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` sends `null`. The server (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`) explicitly defaults a blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, so the persisted record will have a real category. However, on successful save the client does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));` which with `categoryId === null` will set `category` to `undefined/null`, causing the UI (via `{{category-badge host.category}}`) to show a blank category until the record is reloaded/hydrated from the server.
